(i) diversity-dependent diversification is not the default model; (ii) there is little evidence for diversity-dependent diversification; and, (iii) the lack of evidence for diversity-dependent effects is consistent with the idea that the carrying capacities of the environment are time-varying.
the idea of a fixed carrying capacity, and thus a fixed limit on the number of species that can coexist, is not supported by the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a pressing need for explicit modelling of diversity dependence and time-varying species pools, and for a greater emphasis on the ecological context of macro-evolutionary dynamics.
the debate on the role of diversity dependence is not a question of whether diversity dependence is important or not, but how important it is.

there are many ways in which diversity-dependent diversification can be implemented, and that the evidence for and/or against the idea of bound or unbound diversification should be assessed on a clade-by-clade, or even species pool-by-species pool, basis.
